status_vocabulary.supported: the operation is implemented against the real provider API, exercised by tests today, and meets the tracker-contract.md #4.2 target guarantee for its journey family
status_vocabulary.gap: the operation is required by a core journey (operations[].core == true) but is unimplemented, explicitly refused by the adapter, or below the #4.2 target guarantee; blocks V1 exit for that provider until the owner ticket closes it. A non-core operation is never a gap: an unimplemented non-core capability is 'refused' instead
status_vocabulary.refused: the adapter's refusal is deliberate and never blocks V1 exit. Valid ONLY on a non-core operation (operations[].core == false): criterion 1 requires every core operation to reach 'supported', so an unsupported core operation is always 'gap' or 'to_qualify', both of which block V1 exit for that provider
status_vocabulary.to_qualify: the operation's real behaviour against the live provider is not qualified; PAT-65 must qualify it on authorized test resources before any other status can be asserted. On a core operation, 'to_qualify' blocks V1 exit for that provider exactly like 'gap'; only the reason differs (unqualified transport vs. known-missing implementation). On a non-core operation 'to_qualify' is temporary: before V1 exit it must resolve to 'supported' or to 'refused' with a typed refusal (never a bare NotImplementedError), and it names its owner ticket (PAT-65 unless stated)

cell_fields.ticket: owner ticket (PAT-<n>); required on every core 'gap' and 'to_qualify' cell and on every non-core 'to_qualify' cell
cell_fields.blocked_by_adr: id of an entry in pending_adrs; present when closing the cell changes a durable invariant, so no code may land before that ADR is explicitly accepted

ghprojects.note: stub adapter. It overrides resolve_project (a registry.resolve() basename lookup, ghprojects.py:30-32) and the ten abstract methods search, get_issue, create_issue, update_fields, set_state, link, add_comment, list_adrs, create_adr, set_adr_status, each raising NotImplementedError (ghprojects.py:19-24, 34-62). Every other Tracker member is inherited from base.py: optional ports raise their typed unavailability errors, validate_* and preflight_issue_operation are no-ops, resolve_checkout_project falls back to the basename lookup (base.py:135-152). PAT-65 qualifies; PAT-54/57/58/59/64/66/67 implement.

devhub.note: Foundry's internal pilot tracker, not one of the three repository-facing V1 trackers; listed for contrast only: it is the only adapter with epic_closure_supported and epic_subgraph_supported (devhub.py:220-223).

youtrack.evidence: resolve_project is registry.resolve('youtrack', repo) (youtrack.py:260-261). Without a marker, registry.resolve() (registry.py:725-773) looks the entry up by the name it is given, taken from registry.repo_basename() (registry.py:653-664: PROJECT_REPO or the remote's last path segment); with a marker, registry._matching_registry_bindings() (registry.py:298-311) falls back to the basename entry when no canonical_repo matches. YouTrack mutations resolve no binding: write.mutation_project returns None after validate_legacy_mutation (write.py:50-56), and validate_mutation_repository/validate_mutation_project/validate_issue_binding are the base no-ops (base.py:164-184). Two repositories sharing a basename are not distinguished

linear.evidence: resolve_project discards its repo argument (linear.py:1250-1256); resolve_checkout_project and validate_mutation_repository (linear.py:1258-1280) use registry.resolve_canonical_repository (registry.py:800-830), which matches only canonical_repo and fails closed on ambiguity; every issue read or written is asserted to belong to the bound team and project UUIDs (_assert_issue_project, linear.py:2016-2026)

ghprojects.evidence: resolve_project delegates to registry.resolve('ghprojects', repo) (ghprojects.py:30-32), the same basename-keyed lookup as YouTrack; the repository-identity-scoped normalized key a Project v2 issue needs is PAT-65's qualification

open_points_not_decided_here.description: GitHub Projects v2 is GraphQL-only. Foundry's code-host rule is 'Never GraphQL ... REST only — the adapter enforces it' (skills/merge-pr/SKILL.md:226). A repository choosing ghprojects keeps the REST-only GitHub code-host adapter for PRs/merges, but its tracker adapter would need GraphQL. PAT-65 resolves this tension; PAT-53 does not.
